## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bhūridattacariya* ("The Conduct of Bhūridatta") is the twelfth text of the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, situated in the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Bareau; SuttaCentral]. The narrative recounts a previous life in which the Bodhisatta was born as Bhūridatta, endowed with great supernatural powers, who visited the heavenly world alongside the Great King Virūpakkha [Bareau]. In this life, he undertook an unwavering observance of moral virtue (*sīla*), resolutely committing to the "four factors" (*caturo aṅge adhiṭṭhāya*) and choosing to sacrifice his bodily life rather than break his moral vows or harbor anger against those who might attack him with weapons [Bareau; Lim 2009].
